'''Saucer Head''' was the nickname of a [[Gender|male]] [[sabacc]] dealer who operated on [[Vandor]] around [[10 BBY]]. He dealt for a game between the [[smuggler]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], the outlaw [[Han Solo]] and some other players.

==Biography==
[[File:Saucer-Head-Vandor.png|thumb|left|250px|Saucer Head was a sabacc dealer during the Imperial Era]]
Around [[10 BBY]], Saucer Head<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Solo: A Star Wars Story|cardname=Saucer Head|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/176424/cid/11326611}}</ref> was a [[sabacc]] dealer at [[The Lodge]] on [[Vandor]]. He dealt the cards for the famed [[smuggler]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian's]] game, where he was beating all the other players at the table. The outlaw [[Han Solo]] later joined the game and took the seat next to Saucer Head. He began winning every round after he and Calrissian betted their [[starship]]s. During the game, Saucer Head took notice of fellow players [[Susaut Volupicite]] and [[Karjj]], who sat next to him while losing the game to the [[smuggler]]. Calrissian ultimately won the game by cheating, keeping his prized [[YT-1300 light freighter]], the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', with him.<ref name="Solo">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Saucer Head was a male sabacc dealer who could speak [[Cynogan]].<ref name="Solo" />

==Skills and abilities==
In Calrissian and Solo's sabacc game, Saucer Head shuffled the cards around the table with ease.<ref name="Solo" />

==Equipment==
Saucer Head wore a round, [[Color|red]] [[hat]] and a [[Breath mask|breathing mask]] that obscured his face. He also wore a black [[poncho]] and black gloves.<ref name="Solo" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:SaucerHead-Davies.png|thumb|right|160px|Concept art of Saucer Head, by Jake Lunt Davies]]
Saucer Head made his first appearance in the [[2018]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', played by an uncredited actor.<ref name="Solo" /> Magician [[Steven Bridges]] later confirmed that he played the dealer in the film.<ref name="Steven Bridges Solo">{{YouTube|video=WQRi66zb9ww|text=I'M IN STAR WARS!|channel=channel/UCqK0ukwGsTDh7sHih1OmLJA|name=StevenBridges|quote=Talking about my experiences consulting and appearing in Solo: A Star Wars Story. (and yes, I met Donald Glover)}}</ref> He was first named on a card in the [[2018 Topps Solo: A Star Wars Story]] trading card set released by [[Topps|The Topps Company, Inc.]] in 2018.<ref name="Topps" />

Saucer Head was designed for ''Solo'' by [[Jake Lunt Davies]].<ref name="Instagram">{{Instagram|username=jakeluntdavies|url=p/B5ON-JoDHq4|name=[[Jake Lunt Davies]]|date=2019-11-23|quote=This guy I designed for Solo rocked up again in The Mandalorian ep3. Still hanging out in the bounty hunter bar. But a better view on him this time. Shame the havelock and neck cowl were missing. But hey, small quibble. #starwars #themandalorian #saucerhead #bountyhunter #conceptdesign #creaturedesign #solo #soloastarwarsstory|archivedate=20191124062210}}</ref> His design served as a potential design for [[Enfys Nest]], but was later repurposed into the sabacc dealer seen in the film, with [[leather]] replacing the [[bone]] mask.<ref name="Art-Of-Solo" />

Saucer Head's costume was later reused in the [[2019]] television show [[Star Wars: The Mandalorian|''The Mandalorian]].''<ref name="Instagram" />
